Email Integration — how it works, in plain terms

Every email sent to or received by a Siraj shared mailbox is automatically captured and attached to the right customer's file — without anyone having to forward, save, or manually log it.

⚠ This connection needs to be renewed periodically to keep working. IT operations needs to own this after go-live, or capture can quietly stop without anyone noticing for a few days.
How email flows into the CRM
From inbox to customer file, automatically — four stages
Stage 1 · Where emails come in
The shared mailboxes staff already use
No new mailbox, no new habit — staff keep using Outlook exactly as they do today. The CRM simply watches these mailboxes in the background.
sales@sirajfinance.ae credit@sirajfinance.ae cad@sirajfinance.ae tradefinance@sirajfinance.ae
a new email arrives
Stage 2 · What happens automatically
The email is captured and matched to a customer
1The moment an email lands, it's picked up right away — nothing sits waiting to be checked.
2The full email and any attachments are pulled in and matched to the correct customer case, using the case reference in the subject line or the address it was sent to.
3If it can't be matched automatically, it's never silently dropped — it goes to a manual-review queue for the operations team to link by hand.
This runs as its own dedicated process, separate from the rest of the CRM — so a slow email doesn't slow anyone down elsewhere in the system.
Stage 3 · Where it's kept
Stored securely, permanently
The email and its attachments are archived in the CRM's own secure records — separate from anyone's personal inbox. Nothing is ever deleted, even if the original is deleted from Outlook, so the file always has a complete, permanent history for audits.
Stage 4 · What the team sees
It appears on the customer's timeline instantly
The RM, credit team, or compliance officer sees the new email on the customer's timeline right away — alongside every document, WhatsApp message, and compliance action for that case, all in one place.
What needs to happen to turn this on
The rollout, in business terms — who's involved and why it matters
1
Get IT & Risk sign-off for read-only mailbox access
Before anything is built, Siraj IT and Risk need to formally approve giving the CRM read access to the four shared mailboxes. This access is read-only and automated — no individual ever logs into these mailboxes as a person.
2
Connect the shared mailboxes
Once approved, the four mailboxes are connected to the CRM. From this point on, the connection needs to be periodically re-confirmed to keep working — this is an ongoing IT responsibility, not a one-time setup, and it's the most common cause of "emails stopped syncing" if nobody owns it after go-live.
3
Every new email is picked up immediately
There's no waiting or manual checking — the moment an email arrives, it's captured and queued for processing straight away.
4
The full email and attachments are pulled in
The complete email — subject, body, and every attachment — is retrieved so nothing is left partially captured.
5
It's matched to the right customer case
The system reads the case reference from the subject line, or the mailbox address it was sent to, to work out which customer file it belongs to. If it can't tell, the email is routed to the operations team for manual review — never dropped.
6
Everything is filed and kept together
The email and its attachments are stored against that customer's case, with a full record of when it arrived, who it involves, and how it was matched — ready for review at any time.
7
It shows up on the customer's timeline right away
Staff see the new email appear on the customer timeline within moments, without needing to refresh anything — the same as any other update to that case.
8
Nothing is ever deleted
Every captured email stays on record permanently, even if the original is deleted from someone's inbox. That gives Siraj a complete, tamper-proof history for every customer — meeting the legal-hold and audit requirements.
What lands on the customer timeline
Every entry type — email, document, WhatsApp, compliance action — lands on the same timeline regardless of source, exactly as the BRD requires: nothing lives only in an individual mailbox.
